links.outcome: Discrimination of momentary suicidal ideation for personalized (temporal holdout) versus new-individual (subject holdout) models
links.effect: Temporal holdout (personalized) AUC=0.83, AUPRC=0.77; subject holdout near chance (AUC≈0.50). Authors propose personalized VLM monitoring after a calibration period.
links.quote: Screen content predicts short-term SI with clinically meaningful accuracy when models are personalized but does not generalize across individuals.

links.outcome: Generalization of performance to unseen individuals
links.effect: Subject holdout AUC≈0.50 (near chance); a simple lexical screening method retained modest discrimination (AUC=0.62).
links.quote: Subject holdout generalization was near chance (AUC≈0.50), though a simple lexical screening method retained modest discrimination (AUC=0.62).

unlisted_practices: Two-stage architecture: coarse lexical screening for new patients, then personalized monitoring after a calibration period
On-device inference with smaller models for privacy-preserving deployment

screen.reason: The study develops and tests vision-language models for prospective prediction of momentary suicidal ideation using collected smartphone screenshots and EMA data, focusing on model accuracy and personalization challenges rather than evaluating a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
